proof.text: Set A_mu=B_mu/sqrt(s_mu), delta=xB-s and K=sum_4||A_mu^2-I||HS^2+sum_12_ordered||{A_mu,A_nu}||HS^2. Since s_mu^-2<2^14, ||(B_mu^2-x_mu I)+delta_mu I||HS^2<=2||B_mu^2-x_mu I||HS^2+8delta_mu^2. Thus K<=2^15 sum_self_residual+2^14 sum_ordered_cross+2^17||delta||^2<=2^12 T. All four self terms and twelve ordered cross terms are retained.

If T<2^-52 then e=sqrt(K)<2^-20. Each ||A_mu||op<=sqrt(1+e)<2. Define F1=sign(A1). Invertibility follows ||A1^2-I||op<=e<1. Scalar |lambda-sign(lambda)|<=|lambda^2-1| gives ||A1-F1||HS<=e. Tr A1=0 and |Tr(F1-A1)|<=2e<2 force Tr F1=0, since Tr F1 is an even integer. This is rank two plus/rank two minus, proved rather than assumed.

For j=2,3,4 define P_k(X)=(X-F_k X F_k)/2 for k<j, C_j=P_1...P_(j-1)(A_j), and F_j=sign(C_j). Existing F_k are Hermitian involutions and pairwise anticommute, so their conjugations commute. Each P_k is HS-orthogonal projection and an operator-norm contraction. Thus C_j is Hermitian and anticommutes with EVERY preceding F_k. Let h_j=||A_j-C_j||HS and r_k=||A_k-F_k||HS. Telescoping the commuting contraction product gives h_j<=sum_(k<j) ||{A_j,F_k}||HS/2 <=(j-1)e/2+2sum_(k<j)r_k. Also ||C_j^2-I||HS<=e+4h_j. If this is<1, C_j is invertible; odd functional calculus sign(C_j) preserves every anticommutation, and r_j<=h_j+||C_j^2-I||HS<=e+5h_j. No inference from merely small independent residuals is used.

Induction gives r_1<=e, r_2<=14e, r_3<=156e, r_4<=1719e. The largest h_j bound is h_4<=343.5e and largest square defect is<=1375e<1 at e<2^-20. Earlier h_2<=2.5e and h_3<=31e likewise suffice. Sum r_j^2<=2979494 K<2^22 K. Consequently sum_mu||B_mu-sqrt(s_mu)F_mu||HS^2<2^23 K<=2^35 T, using max s_mu<2.

The four exact F_mu obey F_mu F_nu+F_nu F_mu=2delta_mu_nu I. Every nonempty ordered product word has zero trace: conjugation by a suitable F_mu reverses its sign. The sixteen product words are therefore HS-orthogonal and span M4(C), so the representation is irreducible. The corresponding native Gamma words give the same complex *-algebra. Explicitly S(X)=1/16 sum_(all16subsets) F_word X Gamma_word^dagger is the orthogonal intertwiner projection for the common signed Clifford word group. Its image has dimension one; at least one of the sixteen S(E_ab) is nonzero. Such T0 obeys F_mu T0=T0 Gamma_mu and T0^dagger T0=alpha I, alpha=Tr(T0^dagger T0)/4>0. U0=T0/sqrt(alpha) is unitary. Multiply by any fourth root of det(U0)^-1 to obtain U in SU4; all F_mu=U Gamma_mu Udagger simultaneously. The common stabilizer is scalars intersect SU4=Z4. Thus orbit is SU4/Z4, not independent component or SO4 frames.

For T>=2^-52, allow zero/missing components, wrong ranks and arbitrarily large B. Compare to any fixed native C in O_s. Sum s_mu<4, so ||C||tupleHS^2<16; ||B||tupleHS^2=4sum x_mu<16+8||delta||. Hence dist^2(B,O_s)<=2||B||^2+2||C||^2<64+16||delta||<=64+2sqrt(T). Since sqrt(T)<=2^26 T and 64<=2^58 T on this branch, dist^2< (2^58+2^27)T<2^59 T. This is a POINTWISE expectation price, not probability times an unbounded radius. Combining with the good branch proves the global theorem.

For every originating configuration/root/partition in the SAME nu, triangle and (a+b)^2<=2a^2+2b^2 give dist^2(Phi^tree,O_s)<=2||Phi^tree-B||tupleHS^2+2dist^2(B,O_s). Integrate without replacing field/occupation correlations, conditioning on separate good configurations or freezing B. This proves d_orbit<=2d2+2^60 E T<=2d2+2^61 eta. The exact canonical rho_N remains the original disintegration weight. Tree covariance is unitary, so scalar distance is gauge invariant.

O_s is compact. The nearest-orbit set M(Phi) is nonempty compact with closed graph; a Borel selector exists in this finite-dimensional Polish setting. The exact distance and minimizer-set relation are dist(VPhi Vdagger,O_s)=dist(Phi,O_s) and M(VPhi Vdagger)=V M(Phi)Vdagger. A Borel U representative exists via compact-fibre measurable selection, modulo Z4; equivalently select the first nonzero word-averaged matrix unit and a principal determinant fourth root on the constructive good branch. That branch's tuple F is conjugation-equivariant. No globally equivariant single tuple selector is possible at Phi=0, whose full SU4 stabilizer fixes no point in this orbit. Arbitrary nearest Borel selectors remain valid for the norm bound; covariance claims concern the set/distance, not an unjustified unique selector. No differentiable global selection or derivative graph is supplied.
